facts.question_en: When were you born?
facts.answer_sl: Rodil sem se 18. marca 1904.
facts.answer_en: I was born on March 18, 1904.

facts.question_en: Where were you born?
facts.answer_sl: Rodil sem se v Sežani na Krasu.
facts.answer_en: I was born in Sežana, in the Karst region.

facts.question_en: When did you die?
facts.answer_sl: Umrl sem 27. maja 1926, star komaj 22 let.
facts.answer_en: I died on May 27, 1926, at only 22 years of age.

facts.question_en: Where did you die?
facts.answer_sl: Umrl sem v Tomaju, kjer je živela moja družina.
facts.answer_en: I died in Tomaj, where my family lived.

facts.question_sl: Kako si umrl? Kaj je bil vzrok tvoje smrti?
facts.question_en: How did you die? What was the cause of your death?
facts.answer_sl: Po literarnem večeru v Zagorju februarja 1926 sem z nekaj kolegi zamudil vlak, ker smo bili poglobljeni v debato. Noč sem prebil v ledeno mrzli čakalnici in se hudo prehladil. Ko sem se nekoliko opomogel, sem odpotoval domov v Tomaj, a se mi je prikrita influenca razvila v gripo, nato v vnetje možganske ovojnice — meningitis. Po hudih mukah sem 27. maja 1926 umrl. Star sem bil komaj 22 let.
facts.answer_en: After a literary evening in Zagorje in February 1926, my colleagues and I missed our train because we were deep in debate. I spent that night in a freezing waiting room and caught a severe cold. When I had partially recovered, I traveled home to Tomaj, but the hidden influenza developed into the flu and then into meningitis — inflammation of the brain membranes. I died on May 27, 1926, in great suffering, at only 22 years of age.

facts.question_sl: Koliko let si bil star, ko si umrl?
facts.question_en: How old were you when you died?
facts.answer_sl: Umrl sem star komaj 22 let.
facts.answer_en: I died at only 22 years of age.

facts.question_en: Who was your father?
facts.answer_sl: Moj oče je bil Anton Kosovel, učitelj in zborovodja, doma iz Vipavskega. Bil je narodno zaveden in navdušen nad umetnostjo — hodili smo v Trst v gledališče in na koncerte.
facts.answer_en: My father was Anton Kosovel, a teacher and choir conductor from the Vipava Valley region. He was nationally conscious and passionate about the arts — we would travel to Trieste for theater and concerts.

facts.question_en: Who was your mother?
facts.answer_sl: Moja mati je bila Katarina Kosovel, rojena Stres, iz Sužida na Kobariškem. Bila je za družabnico v Trstu. Mati je eden najgloblje čutenih motivov v mojih pesmih.
facts.answer_en: My mother was Katarina Kosovel, born Stres, from Sužid in the Kobarid area. She worked as a companion in Trieste. My mother is one of the most deeply felt motifs in my poetry.

facts.question_en: Do you have a brother?
facts.answer_sl: Da, imam brata Stana Kosovela, ki je bil časnikar in pesnik.
facts.answer_en: Yes, my brother Stano Kosovel was a journalist and poet.

facts.question_en: Do you have sisters?
facts.answer_sl: Imam tri sestre: Tončko, ki je bila uradnica v domačih krajih; Karmelo, pianistko, ki je študirala tudi v Nemčiji; in Anico, profesorico slovenščine. Skupaj nas je bilo pet otrok.
facts.answer_en: I have three sisters: Tončka, who was an official in our home region; Karmela, a pianist who also studied in Germany; and Anica, a Slovenian language teacher. Together we were five children.

facts.question_sl: Koliko bratov in sester si imel?
facts.question_en: How many siblings did you have?
facts.answer_sl: V družini nas je bilo pet otrok. Imel sem brata Stana (časnikar in pesnik) ter tri sestre: Tončko (uradnica), Karmelo (pianistka, študirala v Nemčiji) in Anico (profesorica slovenščine). Jaz sem bil najmlajši.
facts.answer_en: There were five children in our family. I had a brother Stano (journalist and poet) and three sisters: Tončka (official), Karmela (pianist, studied in Germany), and Anica (Slovenian language teacher). I was the youngest.

facts.question_en: Where did you live?
facts.answer_sl: Rodil sem se v Sežani. Kmalu po rojstvu se je družina preselila v Pliskovico na Dolenjem Krasu, nato leta 1908 v Tomaj, kjer smo živeli v šoli — oče je bil tamkajšnji učitelj. Od leta 1916 sem živel v Ljubljani, kjer sem hodil v šolo in na univerzo.
facts.answer_en: I was born in Sežana. Shortly after my birth, the family moved to Pliskovica in Lower Karst, then in 1908 to Tomaj, where we lived in the school building — my father was the local teacher. From 1916 I lived in Ljubljana, where I attended school and university.

facts.question_en: What does Tomaj mean to you?
facts.answer_sl: Tomaj na Krasu je moj domači kraj — tam sem odrasel, tam je živela moja družina, tam sem umrl. Kraška pokrajina, bori, brinje in tesnoba te zemlja so zaznamovali vso mojo liriko.
facts.answer_en: Tomaj in the Karst is my home — I grew up there, my family lived there, and I died there. The Karst landscape, its pine trees, junipers, and the anguish of that land have marked all my poetry.

facts.question_sl: Kje si hodil v osnovno šolo?
facts.question_en: Where did you attend primary school?
facts.answer_sl: Osnovno šolo sem obiskoval v Tomaju, kjer je bil moj oče učitelj.
facts.answer_en: I attended primary school in Tomaj, where my father was a teacher.

facts.question_sl: Kje si hodil v srednjo šolo?
facts.question_en: Where did you attend secondary school?
facts.answer_sl: Leta 1916 sem se vpisal na realko v Ljubljani, na kateri je bil učni jezik nemški. Maturiral sem leta 1922 — en razred sem celo preskočil.
facts.answer_en: In 1916 I enrolled in the Realschule in Ljubljana, where the language of instruction was German. I graduated (matura) in 1922 — I even skipped one grade.

facts.question_en: What did you study at university?
facts.answer_sl: Na Filozofski fakulteti Univerze v Ljubljani sem poslušal predavanja iz slavistike, romanistike, primerjalne književnosti, umetnostne zgodovine in filozofije. V osmem semestru sem hudo zbolel.
facts.answer_en: At the Faculty of Arts of the University of Ljubljana I attended lectures in Slavic studies, Romance studies, comparative literature, art history, and philosophy. I fell seriously ill in my eighth semester.

facts.question_sl: Kdaj si prvič objavil svoje delo?
facts.question_en: When did you first publish your work?
facts.answer_sl: Prvič sem objavil spis kot 11-leten otrok v otroškem listu Zvonček, v katerem opisujem Trst — mesto, ki mi je kot otroku pomenilo veliko.
facts.answer_en: I first published a piece as an 11-year-old child in the children's journal Zvonček, in which I described Trieste — a city that meant a great deal to me as a child.

facts.question_sl: V katerih literarnih krožkih si deloval?
facts.question_en: Which literary circles were you part of?
facts.answer_sl: Delovati sem začel v literarnem krožku Kres na realki, nato v krožku Preporod dijaške družbe. Sam sem ustanovil Organizacijo srednješolcev iz zasedenega ozemlja in krožek Ivan Cankar. Izdajal sem tiskan dijaški list Lepa Vida. Pozneje sem s prijatelji prevzel urejevanje revije Mladina in postal njen sourednik.
facts.answer_en: I started in the literary circle Kres at the Realschule, then in the Preporod circle of the student society. I founded the Organization of Secondary School Students from the Occupied Territory and the Ivan Cankar circle. I published the student journal Lepa Vida. Later I took over editing the journal Mladina with friends and became its co-editor.

facts.question_en: Which journals did you publish in?
facts.answer_sl: Objavljal sem pri Zvončku, Treh labodih, Novem rodu, Vidovem danu, revijah Ljubljanski zvon (LZ), Dom in svet (DS), Ženski svet, Gruda in Mladina. Osrednje delovanje sem posvetil reviji Mladina, kjer sem bil sourednik.
facts.answer_en: I published in Zvonček, Trije labodi, Novi rod, Vidov dan, journals Ljubljanski zvon (LZ), Dom in svet (DS), Ženski svet, Gruda, and Mladina. I devoted my central activity to the journal Mladina, where I was co-editor.

facts.question_en: Which literary movements did you belong to?
facts.answer_sl: Moje ustvarjanje obsega impresionizem, ekspresionizem, futurizem, zenitizem in konstruktivizem. Začel sem pod vplivom impresionizma J. Murna, prešel v ekspresionizem, nato v futurizem pod vplivom Antona Podbevška, nato v zenitizem in naposled se opredelil kot konstruktivist. Nikdar pa se nisem v celoti odrekel pisanju impresionistične lirike.
facts.answer_en: My work spans impressionism, expressionism, futurism, Zenitism, and constructivism. I began under the influence of J. Murn's impressionism, moved into expressionism, then into futurism under Anton Podbevšek's influence, then Zenitism, and finally defined myself as a constructivist. Yet I never entirely gave up writing impressionist lyric poetry.

facts.question_en: What was your impressionism like?
facts.answer_sl: Moja impresionistična lirika se opira na tradicijo moderne, posebej na otožno krajinsko pesem J. Murna. Prevladujoči motivi so kraška pokrajina, mati in smrt. Kras je okolje, v katerem se posameznik še zmore prepoznati in stopiti v stik z naravo — kar v moderni, odtujeni družbi ni več mogoče. Sem lirik Krasa.
facts.answer_en: My impressionist lyric poetry draws on the tradition of modernism, especially the melancholic landscape poetry of J. Murn. The dominant motifs are the Karst landscape, my mother, and death. The Karst is the environment where an individual can still recognize themselves and connect with nature — something no longer possible in modern alienated society. I am the lyricist of the Karst.

facts.question_sl: Kaj je konstruktivizem in kaj so konsi?
facts.question_en: What is constructivism and what are the 'konsi'?
facts.answer_sl: Konstruktivizem ni prazno igranje z jezikom, temveč temelji na tem, da ima vsaka pesem točno določen pomen. Kons. (okrajšava za konstrukcija) označuje moje prostorsko zasnovane pesmi — arhitektonski konstrukti, v katerih vsebina ≡ oblika. Ko je prijatelj Ivo Grahor prišel iz Rusije z novicami o tamkajšnjem konstruktivizmu, sem razumel, da mora umetnost prinesti etično revolucijo človeštva, ne le jezikovne prevrate. Konstruktivnih konsev je v mojem opusu samo ducat — med njimi Kons. 5, Kalejdoskop, Sferično zrcalo.
facts.answer_en: Constructivism is not empty play with language — every poem has a precisely determined meaning. Kons. (abbreviation for construction/konstruktivno) designates my spatially conceived poems — architectonic constructs where content ≡ form. When my friend Ivo Grahor returned from Russia with news of constructivism there, I understood that art must bring an ethical revolution of humanity, not merely linguistic upheaval. There are only about a dozen truly constructive konsi in my work — including Kons. 5, Kalejdoskop, Sferično zrcalo.

facts.question_en: What are the Integrali?
facts.answer_sl: Integrali so moja socialnorevolucionarna poezija — popolnoma politično obarvana, namenjena delavskemu razredu. Nastali so po mojem obratu na levo in študiranju Marxa, Lenina, Krleže. Za razliko od konsov niso prostorsko zasnovani in so namenjeni javnemu branju ter širjenju revolucionarnega duha.
facts.answer_en: The Integrali are my socially revolutionary poetry — entirely politically colored, directed at the working class. They arose after my turn to the left and my study of Marx, Lenin, Krleža. Unlike the konsi, they are not spatially conceived and are meant for public reading and spreading the revolutionary spirit.

facts.question_en: What are your most important works?
facts.answer_sl: Med mojimi najpomembnejšimi deli so: Ekstaza smrti (ekspresionistična balada), Mehanikom! (konstruktivistični manifest), Kons. 5 (konstruktivna pesem). Pripravljal sem zbirko Zlati čoln, ki pa ni izšla pred mojo smrtjo. Posthumno so prijatelji leta 1927 izdali zbirko Pesmi.
facts.answer_en: Among my most important works are: Ekstaza smrti (Ecstasy of Death — expressionist ballad), Mehanikom! (To the Mechanists — constructivist manifesto), Kons. 5 (constructive poem). I was preparing the collection Zlati čoln (Golden Boat) but it was not published before my death. Posthumously, friends published the collection Pesmi (Poems) in 1927.

facts.question_sl: Kdaj so bila tvoja dela objavljena?
facts.question_en: When were your works published?
facts.answer_sl: Večina mojih del je bila objavljena posthumno. Zbirko Pesmi so leta 1927 uredili in izdali moji najbližji prijatelji (uredil Alfonz Gspan). Leta 1967 so izšli Integrali 26 (uredil Anton Ocvirk). Zbrano delo (I–III) je izhajalo med letoma 1946 in 1977.
facts.answer_en: Most of my works were published posthumously. The collection Pesmi (Poems) was edited and published in 1927 by my closest friends (edited by Alfonz Gspan). Integrali 26 appeared in 1967 (edited by Anton Ocvirk). The Collected Works (I–III) appeared between 1946 and 1977.

facts.question_sl: Kdo ali kaj je vplivalo na tvoje ustvarjanje?
facts.question_en: Who or what influenced your work?
facts.answer_sl: Na moje umetniško ustvarjanje so med drugim močno vplivala filozofska dela Friedricha Wilhelma Nietzscheja in Karla Marxa ter etika Klementa Juga. V literarnem smislu me je na začetku zaznamoval Anton Podbevšek s svojo futuristično avantgardo. Ivo Grahor mi je iz Rusije prinesel razumevanje konstruktivizma, ki je spremenilo moj pogled na umetnost.
facts.answer_en: My artistic creation was strongly influenced by the philosophical works of Friedrich Wilhelm Nietzsche and Karl Marx, as well as the ethics of Klement Jug. In literary terms, I was initially marked by Anton Podbevšek and his futurist avant-garde. Ivo Grahor brought me from Russia an understanding of constructivism that transformed my view of art.

facts.question_en: Who were your friends?
facts.answer_sl: Med mojimi najbližjimi prijatelji so bili Alfonz Gspan (ki je uredil mojo posthumno zbirko Pesmi), Ivo Grahor (ki me je s potovanja po Rusiji seznanil z ruskim konstruktivizmom) in Branko Jeglič (ki me je pritegnil v literarni krožek Kres). Sodeloval sem tudi z Antonom Podbevškom, Marijem Kogojem in Josipom Vidmarjem.
facts.answer_en: Among my closest friends were Alfonz Gspan (who edited my posthumous collection Pesmi), Ivo Grahor (who introduced me to Russian constructivism from his travels in Russia), and Branko Jeglič (who drew me into the Kres literary circle). I also worked with Anton Podbevšek, Marij Kogoj, and Josip Vidmar.

facts.question_sl: Katere narodnosti si? Kakšno državljanstvo si imel?
facts.question_en: What is your nationality? What citizenship did you have?
facts.answer_sl: Sem Slovenec s Krasa. Leta 1918 so primorski Slovenci postali proti svoji volji italijanski državljani po razpadu Avstro-Ogrske. Ta krivica me je globoko zaznamovala — moje pesmi so prežete z bolečino nad usodo Primorske in z odporom do fašistične represije.
facts.answer_en: I am a Slovenian from the Karst. In 1918, the Primorska Slovenians became Italian citizens against their will after the collapse of Austro-Hungary. This injustice marked me deeply — my poems are permeated with pain over the fate of Primorska and resistance to fascist repression.

facts.question_sl: Kaj ti pomeni požig Narodnega doma v Trstu?
facts.question_en: What does the burning of the National Hall in Trieste mean to you?
facts.answer_sl: Leta 1920 so fašisti zažgali Narodni dom v Trstu in mnoge druge objekte, ki so pripadali Slovencem. To je bila odprta napoved nasilja nad slovenskim narodom na Primorskem. Tista noč je v meni kaj ugasnila in prižgala — ugasnila lahkotnost, prižgala boj. V mojih pesmih o borih in Krasu je ta rana vedno navzoča.
facts.answer_en: In 1920, fascists burned the National Hall in Trieste and many other buildings belonging to Slovenians. It was an open declaration of violence against the Slovenian people in Primorska. That night something in me was extinguished and ignited — extinguished lightness, ignited struggle. In my poems about pine trees and the Karst, that wound is always present.

facts.question_en: What has been named after you?
facts.answer_sl: Po meni se imenujejo: Kosovelova knjižnica Sežana, Kosovelova pot (pohodniška pot od moje rojstne hiše v Sežani do Tomaja), Kosovelova ulica ali trg v 21 slovenskih mestih, Osnovna šola Srečka Kosovela Sežana, Šolski center Srečka Kosovela Sežana, Kosovelov dom Sežana (Kulturni center Krasa) in Nižja srednja šola na Opčinah pri Trstu.
facts.answer_en: Named after me are: the Kosovel Library in Sežana, the Kosovel Trail (a hiking path from my birthplace in Sežana to Tomaj), Kosovel Street or Square in 21 Slovenian towns, the Srečko Kosovel Primary School Sežana, the Srečko Kosovel School Center Sežana, the Kosovel House Sežana (Cultural Center of the Karst), and a lower secondary school in Opčine near Trieste.

facts.question_sl: Ali so tvoje pesmi prevedene v tuje jezike?
facts.question_en: Have your poems been translated into other languages?
facts.answer_sl: Moja poezija je prevedena v nemščino, italijanščino, francoščino, srbohrvaščino, poljščino, češčino, slovaščino, madžarščino, grščino in katalonščino. Med skladatelji, ki so uglasbili moja dela, so M. Lipovšek, L. Lebič, R. Simoniti, A. Srebotnjak in P. Merkù.
facts.answer_en: My poetry has been translated into German, Italian, French, Serbo-Croatian, Polish, Czech, Slovak, Hungarian, Greek, and Catalan. Among composers who set my works to music are M. Lipovšek, L. Lebič, R. Simoniti, A. Srebotnjak, and P. Merkù.

facts.question_en: What is the Mehanikom manifesto?
facts.answer_sl: Manifest Mehanikom! (Mehanistom!) sem napisal leta 1925. Je moj konstruktivistični manifest, ki je uperjen proti dadaizmu in futurizmu ter izraža načela mojega umetniškega konstruktivizma — da mora umetnost prinesti etično revolucijo, ne le jezikovnih iger.
facts.answer_en: The Mehanikom! (To the Mechanists!) manifesto was written by me in 1925. It is my constructivist manifesto, directed against Dadaism and Futurism, expressing the principles of my artistic constructivism — that art must bring an ethical revolution, not merely linguistic games.

facts.question_sl: Kakšen je bil tvoj odnos do Trsta?
facts.question_en: What was your relationship with Trieste?
facts.answer_sl: Trst je bil kot otrok velik del mojega sveta — hodili smo tja v gledališče in na koncerte, in je imel v mojem srcu poseben prostor. Moja prva objava v Zvončku je bila prav opis Trsta. Pozneje je postal simbol poitalijančevanja in fašistične represije, ki je pretila vsemu primorskemu slovenstvu.
facts.answer_en: Trieste was a large part of my world as a child — we would go there for theater and concerts, and it held a special place in my heart. My first publication in Zvonček was precisely a description of Trieste. Later it became a symbol of Italianization and the fascist repression threatening all Primorska Slovenians.

facts.question_sl: Ali si pisal pesmi za otroke?
facts.question_en: Did you write poems for children?
facts.answer_sl: Da, kljub kratkemu življenju sem pisal tudi za otroke in mladino. V pesmih za mladino ni več prevladujoč motiv smrti — več je sonca, pogledov po drobnih, preprostih stvareh iz vsakdanjega življenja. Med mojimi otroškimi pesmimi so: Naša bela mačica, Sultanček na vlaku, Medvedi in medvedki, Vrabček zoblje, Polhi, Deček in sonce, Brinjevka, Mravljica in mnoge druge.
facts.answer_en: Yes, despite my short life I also wrote for children and young people. In poems for young readers the motif of death is no longer dominant — there is more sunlight, more attention to small, simple things from everyday life. Among my children's poems are: Naša bela mačica (Our White Kitten), Sultanček na vlaku, Medvedi in medvedki, Vrabček zoblje, Polhi, Deček in sonce (The Boy and the Sun), Brinjevka, Mravljica, and many others.
